statement: For full-dimensional A1,A2⊂Z² with Qi=conv(Ai), the A1-degree of the mixed-discriminant cycle is area(Q2)+2MV(Q1,Q2)−Σ_(e,f) min{u(e,A1),u(f,A2)} length(f)−Σ_(v vertex of A1) mm(v). The first sum is over strongly parallel edges; mm(v)=MV(Q1,Q2)−MV(conv(A1 minus {v}),Q2), and u is subdiagram volume. Interchanging 1,2 gives the second degree.

answer.text: Gives the explicit two-variable mixed-discriminant cycle bidegree in terms of mixed areas, parallel-edge subdiagram volumes and vertex mixed multiplicities.

notes:
The theorem gives the cycle Δ̃=Δ^i(A), not automatically the reduced polynomial degree. Divide cycle degrees by the Cayley configuration’s lattice index to obtain reduced degrees. Areas use the source’s lattice normalization.
